TICKET DETAILS

Calculation notes

Reporting period and scope

Tickets belong to the month of their Create Date in Saudi Arabia time (UTC+03:00). Previous-month and prior-year comparisons use the same filters. Months outside the source’s date range are unavailable.

Power BI monthly uses the attached report’s Monthly Overview (SA) scope: blank Parent TT and its explicit root cause exclusions. Service impact remains selectable. All recorded faults removes the parent and root cause exclusions. Neither scope automatically excludes SLA exemptions from ticket volume.

Volume, restoration and SLA

Ticket volume counts distinct ticket numbers. A ticket/site pair is stored once; duplicate snapshots retain the most complete row, then the latest cleared date, then the earliest source row. Regional ticket counts can overlap if future files link one ticket to several sites.

Recorded restoration hours = sum of the workbook’s RestorationTime HHMMSS × 24. Mean restoration = total valid recorded minutes ÷ records with a recorded duration. Missing durations are excluded from these two measures and counted separately. Recorded zero durations remain zero.

SLA compliance = non-breached ÷ eligible records. Eligible records have an explicit Yes/No in Exceed SLA and are not marked Exclude/Excluded in the SLA column. Missing SLA outcomes are excluded. Source SLA decisions are preserved, including cases with historical date inconsistencies.

Service interruption hours use Service Impact Finish − Service Impact Start where both dates exist and the interval is nonnegative. These are ticket intervals; overlapping intervals are not merged and are not network availability. Availability requires a historical on-air inventory denominator, which was not supplied.

Source limitations

The PBIX report layout and monthly exclusion list were read. Its compressed VertiPaq data and DAX expressions were not decoded. The web page uses the supplied outage workbook, so exact equality with the PBIX measure New Duration Dax Min has not been established.

Source date inconsistencies and recorded durations that differ from create-to-clear time remain visible in the data checks. The original workbook is unchanged. No automatic refresh from RTTS or Power BI is configured.
